asOf: Updated Fri 09 Oct 2026, 09:18 Dubai · prices from 2026-10-08 close · for the Fri 09 Oct session
kicker: Dubai desk · US open 5:30pm Dubai (9:30am ET)
notes: Risk-off tone into Friday: Nasdaq 100 suffered its worst day in seven weeks on Thursday (-1.4%) and a chipmaker gauge slumped 3.4% after a Financial Times report revived doubts about OpenAI's revenue and the sustainabili
Treasury yields remain elevated, with the 10-year hovering near multi-decade highs (~5.2-5.3%) and the 30-year near 5.6%, pressuring high-multiple growth and tech names.

Oil is the swing factor: Brent spiked above $104-105 and WTI near $92-93 after reports the White House asked the Pentagon to prep Iran strike options before the midterms; Trump later said strikes won't come before the mi
Crypto is soft in sympathy with the risk-off/rate backdrop: Bitcoin slipped to roughly $81,000-$82,000, down from recent highs, as the broader crypto market cap fell about 2.5%.
Q3 earnings season is just beginning (big banks start the week of Oct 12), with FactSet projecting ~29.5% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth, which would be a third straight quarter above 25% if realized.
calendar: Delta Air Lines (DAL) reported Q3 results before Friday's open and topped estimates, with shares already reacting positively intraday Thursday into the print.
PepsiCo (PEP) reported Thursday morning with an EPS beat and raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to the high end of its range.
Levi Strauss (LEVI) reported Wednesday after the close; EPS beat (helped by tariff refunds) but revenue missed and guidance was trimmed, sending shares sharply lower into Thursday/Friday.
CMS released 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings on Oct 8, causing a major divergence: Humana (HUM) surged on a rating upgrade while Alignment Healthcare (ALHC) tumbled on a downgrade.
Two Nasdaq IPOs are pricing/starting to trade this week: TRex Bio (TRXB, Eli Lilly-backed biotech) and Retension Pharmaceuticals (RTSN), both listing around Oct 9.
Geopolitical risk remains a live catalyst for energy/oil-sensitive names: reports of potential US strikes on Iran before the Nov 3 midterms are driving crude volatility.

avoid.reason: Shares fell sharply despite an EPS beat because the beat leaned on a one-time tariff refund while revenue missed and the company narrowed its full-year revenue growth outlook to the low end on U.S. DTC weakness.

Webull plunged roughly 20-30% this week after a bipartisan House committee report found the brokerage structurally tied to China's government, triggering multiple shareholder securities-law investigations.
Alignment Healthcare tumbled over 20% after CMS's newly published 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings showed a sharp reversal lower for the insurer, the opposite move seen in rival Humana.
Micron is at the center of the AI-capex-doubt selloff that sank the Nasdaq 100's chipmaker gauge 3.4% on fears about OpenAI's revenue sustainability and the broader AI spending boom.

items.name: Humana Inc.
items.news: Humana's largest Medicare Advantage contract (H5216) was upgraded from 3.5 to 4 stars in CMS's newly released 2027 Star Ratings, restoring eligibility for federal quality bonus payments. Shares surged as much as 13-16% after the Oct 8 announcement, with Cantor Fitzgerald also upgrading the stock to Overweight citing improved Stars confidence.
items.risk: A large portion of the positive catalyst may already be priced in after the after-hours spike, and the ratings impact payments only starting in 2028.
items.entry: Dip to $379.53–384.84, or break above $410.01 on volume

items.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
items.news: Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral on Oct 8 with a $230 price target (~18% upside), citing expanding demand for sovereign AI and custom applications, a day after another analyst initiated coverage at $250.
items.risk: Valuation remains extremely rich (roughly 50x forward sales), and the stock is trading within a broader AI-sector selloff tied to OpenAI revenue doubts.
items.entry: Dip to $195.87–197.91, or break above $204.44 on volume

items.name: Delta Air Lines Inc.
items.news: Delta reported Q3 2026 results before Friday's open; reported EPS of $2.01 came in well above the softened consensus near $1.76-1.88 amid elevated fuel-cost concerns, and shares were already up nearly 4% intraday as the print approached.
items.risk: Rising oil prices from Middle East tensions are a direct fuel-cost headwind for airlines, and the stock has historically shown mixed one-day earnings reactions (roughly 40% positive over the last 5 years).
items.entry: Dip to $80.91–81.77, or break above $86.17 on volume

items.name: Marvell Technology Inc.
items.news: TD Cowen upgraded Marvell to Buy from Hold on Oct 7 and raised its price target 43% to $350 from $245, arguing the company's fundamental growth drivers have shifted to its strong connectivity franchise.
items.risk: Semiconductor names are at the epicenter of the current AI-capex-doubt selloff; a chipmaker gauge fell 3.4% Thursday, so sentiment risk is elevated.
items.entry: Dip to $267.79–272.60, or break above $301.27 on volume

items.name: Illumina Inc.

items.risk: Genomics/life-science tools names can be sensitive to biotech funding sentiment and broader risk-off moves in growth stocks.
items.entry: Dip to $256.91–262.27, or break above $309.35 on volume

items.name: Exxon Mobil Corp.
items.news: Brent crude jumped more than 4% this week and WTI rose similarly after reports the White House asked the Pentagon to prepare Iran strike options before the midterms, pushing Brent above $104-105 a barrel before Trump said strikes won't come before the elections.
items.risk: Oil-driven moves can reverse quickly on diplomatic headlines or de-escalation signals, as already seen when Trump's comments pulled Brent back from session highs.
items.entry: Dip to $166.73–167.97, or break above $169.19 on volume

items.name: PepsiCo Inc.
items.news: PepsiCo's Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.34 beat the $2.29 consensus, and management guided full-year 2026 net revenue to the high end of its range, up approximately 6%, aided by tariff refunds of $178 million in the quarter.
items.risk: Consumer staples carry lower day-trade beta, and the stock already reacted to the print on Thursday, limiting fresh momentum into Friday.
items.entry: Dip to $127.09–127.96, or break above $129.50 on volume

items.name: Grab Holdings Ltd.
items.news: Grab's Q2 revenue grew 21.7% to $997 million, beating estimates, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 16.9% from 13.3% and continued share buybacks supporting the stock even as shares trade near $3.
items.risk: Shares are down nearly 38% year-to-date and remain sensitive to Southeast Asia macro conditions and competitive pressure in ride-hailing/delivery.
items.entry: Dip to $3.05–3.09, or break above $3.23 on volume

items.risk: NIO trades near 52-week lows and remains a high cash-burn Chinese EV name exposed to competitive and geopolitical/ADR risk.
